coverage: Reviewed the upstream common role prompt and all 8 criteria, all five prompts, and the accumulated PDFs; checked the supplied Award, PERB decision, comparator disclosure, Douglas, D.C. Code, Misco, W.R. Grace, and the 2009 appellate opinion at the relevant passages. The packet does not contain the collective-bargaining agreement or a ruling on Braddock’s petition, so ultimate success cannot be established.

findings.title: Criterion fixes the recommendation at petitioning regardless of legal assessment
findings.explanation: The prompt requires a definite yes-or-no recommendation, not a petition. PERB has affirmed; the Award retains a serious suspension and reinstates the officer, and the out-of-record Kucera comparator weakens MPD’s factor-six attack. A careful litigator could conclude that petitioning is not worth the cost and low odds while fully analyzing both exceptions. The criterion would fail that permissible conclusion.

evidence.quote: close with a recommendation on whether MPD should petition for review, stated as a definite position
MPD should petition the DCCA for review
penalty of termination is reduced to a 45-day suspension without pay

findings.suggested_fix: Credit either definite recommendation when it follows a source-grounded assessment of both exceptions and the new comparator.

findings.title: Rubric prescribes a single principal public-policy weakness
findings.explanation: The 45-day suspension is a sensible weakness to identify, but a lawyer could regard the absence of a clearly documented, well-defined policy in the uploaded packet, or the difficulty showing that reinstatement itself violates it, as the principal weakness. Those are reasonable ways to apply W.R. Grace and Misco. The criterion can fail a well-supported alternative ranking.

evidence.quote: principal weakness ... Award imposes serious discipline rather than excusing the misconduct
identify the principal weakness of each argument

findings.suggested_fix: Credit a reasoned principal weakness tied to the governing public-policy test, including the 45-day discipline point.

findings.title: Mandatory burden conclusion goes beyond the uploaded rule
findings.explanation: Douglas requires deference to agency penalty choice but expressly places the ultimate burden of persuasion on the agency and calls for evidence supporting the facts on which penalty selection rests. It does not decide, in terms, how to prove similarity when the agency itself invokes comparators. The uploaded § 1606.2 text mentions similar-case consistency but Chapter 16 excludes sworn MPD members under § 1600.2(g). A careful memo could therefore regard the arbitrator’s specific proof demand as a contestable application of Douglas, not definitely beyond its scope. The criterion may fail that qualified conclusion.

evidence.quote: the ultimate burden is upon the agency to persuade the Board of the appropriateness of the penalty imposed
the Department did not prove that the comparator officers were similarly situated
Sworn members of the Metropolitan Police Department

authorities.citation: Douglas v. Veterans Administration, 5 M.S.P.R. 280 (1981), uploaded reprint pp. 332-33
authorities.proposition: Penalty review respects agency discretion, but the agency bears the ultimate burden of persuasion and must support the factual predicates of its penalty choice.
The text lists same-or-similar penalty consistency as a factor but excludes sworn MPD members from Chapter 16.

findings.suggested_fix: Credit a supported, candid assessment of whether the arbitrator demanded more than Douglas permits; do not require a categorical overreach conclusion.
